title: Voice evaluation
description: One listener's verdict on one voice over the sample corpus. NOT A MOS. ITU-T P.800.2 forbids comparing mean-opinion scores across experiments, P.808 removes outliers across raters at |z|>=3.29 which one rater cannot do, and TTS Arena requires 100 votes before publishing a rating at all. This instrument is a within-harness engineering signal: a regression tripwire and a go/no-go on one voice, valid only against another run of this same harness with the same rater, instructions and playback device. It is never reported as a MOS and never compared to a published MOS. The four axes answer questions the CI-runner benchmark left open; two of them (intelligibility, prosody) map onto recognised constructs, one (seams) is a named long-form-TTS artefact, and one (pronunciation) is really text-normalisation correctness with an objective ground truth, which is why an automated ASR round-trip should eventually replace the human on that axis.

schemaVersion.description: The date this schema shape was fixed. A reader that does not know this version must refuse the file rather than guess.

rater.description: Who listened. A verdict with no name behind it cannot be followed up, and two raters disagreeing is a finding rather than a problem.

listeningConditions.description: Headphones, laptop speakers, phone. The same clip is a different clip on each, so the condition is part of the reading.

runs.description: ONE ENTRY A RUN, because the page compares runs and a verdict file that held only one would lose the comparison it was formed from. This replaced a single top-level `subject`/`clips` pair that the page had not written since it gained a model panel.

pairwise.description: A/B votes. Pairwise beats absolute scoring - 'which of these two is better' is a more reliable judgement than scoring one clip out of context, which is why TTS Arena ranks that way.

runId.description: The directory the clips were read from.

benchmarkRunId.description: `<model>__<configSlug>` from the benchmark that voiced these clips. A listening verdict outlives the audio it was formed on, so it has to name the reading that produced it - without this, two verdicts on the same model at different chunk sizes are indistinguishable after the fact.

config.description: The knobs the clips were voiced at, copied from the run manifest so the evaluation stands alone once the clips are gone.

isolated.description: Whether the benchmark reading behind these clips was taken with nothing else voicing. Null for a run that predates the run contract. It does NOT affect the listening verdict - audio is deterministic, so a contended run produces identical clips - but it decides whether the speed figures beside them may be believed.

loadError.description: Set when the run's manifest could not be fetched. A run reported this way is different from a run with nothing judged, and collapsing the two would read as a listener who declined to score it.

subject.description: What was listened to. Copied from the clip manifest so an evaluation stands alone once the clips are gone.

thumb.description: The fast first pass: two dozen clips on one axis in the time four scales take for six. Null means not yet judged.

verdict.description: The one answer the project actually needs. null means not yet judged, which is different from a reject and must never be counted as one.

scores.description: Five-point scales. 3 is the pass mark: a 3 ships, a 2 does not.

intelligibility.description: Could every word be made out without replaying? Answers the benchmark's open question of whether the audio is good enough to publish at all.

pronunciation.description: Names, numbers, acronyms and tickers. The corpus is news summaries, so proper nouns are the load-bearing case and a model that reads them wrong is unusable regardless of how pleasant it sounds. Unlike the other three this is NOT a perceptual judgement - it has an objective ground truth, because the text says what the words are. It sits here only until an automated ASR round-trip replaces it, and a human score on this axis should be read as a placeholder for a measurement.

prosody.description: Sentence rhythm, emphasis and pauses. Does it read like a person reading news, or like a list of words?

seams.description: Are the chunk joins audible? The pipeline splits every summary over 40 words, so a seam is an artefact this project creates and therefore one it owns. 5 means no join could be heard.

defects.description: Where it went wrong, timestamped. This is what turns 'sounds a bit off' into something that can be fixed - a defect without a timestamp cannot be found again.

expected.description: What the text says it should have been.
